title: How a Camera Lens Works in 60 Seconds 📷🔍 #shorts
description:
A camera lens bends light with curved glass so every ray from one point meets again at one point on the sensor, which is why the image lands upside down. A motor slides glass elements to focus, metal blades set the aperture, and each full f-stop smaller lets in half the light. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#camera #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: The picture inside your camera lands on the sensor *upside down*.

steps.label: Bend
steps.text: Curved *glass* slows light down, so each ray *bends* toward the center.

steps.label: Focus point
steps.text: The rays cross and meet again at one *point*, drawing a sharp but *flipped* image.

steps.label: Focus
steps.text: To *focus*, a motor slides glass elements closer to or farther from the *sensor*.

steps.label: Aperture
steps.text: Metal *blades* form the aperture. Each full *f-stop* smaller lets in half the light.

steps.label: Elements
steps.text: Glass bends each *color* a bit differently, so extra *elements* pull the colors back together.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Bend, cross, *focus*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
